detail:
IMPACT (P1): this is the exact failure the ticket mechanism exists to prevent. An auditor that re-finds a defect after a wrong fix is told its finding was recorded; the finding never appears in `ticket.py list`, never appears in harness/TECHNICAL_DEBT.md, and never reaches the projection's open set. The finding dies, and the CLI's success message makes it look filed.
The module docstring says a closure that was wrong must leave both the closing and the reopening visible - but the only way to reopen is a hand-written `reopened` event that nobody is prompted to write.
SUGGESTED FIX: in fold(), a `filed` event arriving for a ticket whose status is not OPEN should set status=OPEN, bump reopens, and append a note ('re-filed by <source> on <date> after closure'). Or, less invasive: file_ticket returns the current status and cmd_file prints a loud warning ('T-xxxx was CLOSED on <date> by <who>: <resolution>. Re-filing does NOT reopen it; run scripts/ticket.py reopen T-xxxx --resolution ...'). Silence is the defect.
Confirmed by direct execution, not by mutation: no test covers a `filed` event after a `closed` one anywhere in tests/test_tickets.py or tests/test_ticket_sync.py - a missing matrix cell (filed x already-closed).
reproduction:
fold()'s `filed` branch calls replace(existing, sources=..., severity=..., ...) and never touches `status`.
  i,_ = file_ticket(kind=DEFECT, severity=P1, title='lookahead in the panel', path='src/x.py',
                    source='lookahead-auditor', reproduction='pytest -k lookahead', at=T0, log=L)
  append([TicketEvent(ticket=i, action='closed', at=T0+1d, source='impl', resolution='fixed',
                      commit='abc1234')], L)
  file_ticket(... same kind/title/path ..., severity=P0, source='guard-auditor',
              reproduction='still reproduces at HEAD', at=T0+5d, log=L)
Observed 2026-09-04: status='closed', is_open=False, reopens=0, closed_at unchanged, open_tickets()==[], and severity silently raised to P0 on a ticket nobody will look at. scripts/ticket.py file prints "already known - recorded guard-auditor as a second source. Independent corroboration is information; it is not a duplicate." and exits 0.
title: A re-filed finding does not reopen a closed ticket, so an auditor's re-discovery is swallowed

detail:
IMPACT (P1): a finding is silently lost, which is the one failure this mechanism exists to prevent. The blast radius is wider than filing: every load() caller - ticket.py list / show / debt / sync, and tests/test_tickets.py::test_the_repositorys_own_ticket_log_is_readable... - raises 'not a ticket event: <file>:<n>' while any other agent is mid-append. The message accuses the append-only log of having been edited, sending the reader after a corruption that is not there.
9 KiB details are ordinary: an auditor pasting a pytest failure or a mutation table exceeds the buffer easily. This repository runs auditors in parallel by design (the gauntlet workflow), so the race is the normal case, not the exotic one.
SUGGESTED FIX: (a) do not let a read failure prevent the write - compute is_new after appending, or tolerate a read error there; (b) take an fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) around the append and an flock(LOCK_SH) around read_events; (c) write each event with a single os.write() to an O_APPEND fd so the kernel makes it atomic. store.append's docstring claims 'two agents filing at once interleave whole lines' - that claim is false above the buffer size and is untested.
No test in tests/test_tickets.py exercises two writers at once.
reproduction:
file_ticket() calls load(log) BEFORE append(), only to compute the cosmetic `is_new` flag. load() raises on any unparseable line, and append() writes events larger than the 8 KiB io buffer in several write() syscalls, so a concurrent reader can observe a half-written line.
  8 processes x 8 file_ticket() calls, each with detail=9000 chars, same log:
  for t in a b c d e f g h; do python writer.py $LOG $t 9000 8 & done; wait
Observed 2026-09-04 (4 trials at 9 KiB / 70 KiB / 200 KiB / 400 KiB details, 8-12 processes): 1-4 of 8 writers aborted with
  TicketError: /tmp/.../events.jsonl:12: not a ticket event: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 73 (char 72)
Each aborted process had NOT yet appended its event, so its finding is gone. The final file was intact in every trial (0 permanently corrupt lines), so this is a read-side tear, not log corruption.
title: Concurrent filing loses a finding: file_ticket reads a torn line another process is writing and aborts before appending

detail:
IMPACT (P2): harness/TECHNICAL_DEBT.md is the human-facing view of the log, and `ticket.py debt --check` cannot notice - it compares generated text to generated text, so a broken table is 'up to date'. One badly-typed --path or a --title pasted with a newline silently truncates the table, hiding every ticket below it.
The escaping is also unguarded: mutating render_debt to drop `.replace('|', '\\|')` on titles leaves the whole ticket suite green (verified 2026-09-04, mutation D01b on a scratch copy), because no ticket in the real log contains a pipe and no unit test constructs one. The only coverage is test_the_debt_file_is_generated_from_the_log_and_is_up_to_date, which compares against a file generated from that same pipe-free log.
SUGGESTED FIX: refuse '\n' and '\r' in title/path/resolution in TicketEvent.__post_init__ (a title with a newline is not a title), escape '|' in `where` too, and add a render_debt unit test with a pipe and a newline in every rendered field.
reproduction:
render_debt() escapes '|' in t.title and t.resolution but not in `where` (t.path + line), and TicketEvent._validate_filed accepts a newline in title, path or resolution.
  file_ticket(kind=FEATURE, severity=P2, title='line one\nline two', path='src/y.py', ...)
  file_ticket(kind=FEATURE, severity=P2, title='ordinary title', path='src/a|b.py', ...)
  print(render_debt(load(log)))
Observed 2026-09-04:
  | `T-484d7589` | P2 | feature | line one
line two | `src/y.py` | 2026-09-01 | 1 |          <- row split; the table ends here
  | `T-41650bb5` | P2 | feature | ordinary title | `src/a|b.py` | 2026-09-01 | 1 |   <- 8 cells, not 7
A newline in a `closed` event's --resolution breaks the 'Closed and accepted' table the same way.
title: render_debt does not escape a pipe in `path`, and nothing refuses a newline in a title, so the generated debt table breaks

detail:
IMPACT (P2): the id is a hash of (kind, title, path) precisely so that several auditors finding one thing produce one ticket with several sources. That property is defeated by a leading './', an absolute path, or the ':LINE' suffix the CLI's own --path help does not forbid - and the failure is silent: each agent is told 'filed', corroboration is lost, and the triage list gains duplicates. An empty path is accepted and renders as an empty `where` cell.
SUGGESTED FIX: normalise in ticket_id (strip a leading './', reject an absolute path or make it relative to the repo root, strip a trailing ':digits'), and refuse an empty path in _validate_filed - the CLI already makes --path required, so an empty one is a mistake every time. Note this changes existing ids, so it needs a decision about the 15 tickets already in the log.
Related: with no length bound on path, a >2704-byte path wedges the Postgres projection - filed separately.
reproduction:
ticket_id() strips but does not normalise the path, and _validate_filed() does not check it at all.
  file_ticket(..., path='')             -> ACCEPTED T-cfa7855a
  file_ticket(..., path='   ')          -> ACCEPTED T-cfa7855a  (same ticket as '')
  file_ticket(..., path='not a file at all') -> ACCEPTED
  file_ticket(..., path='/etc/passwd')  -> ACCEPTED
and, for one title 'sync loses a row' against one real file:
  'src/trading_platform/tickets/store.py'                       -> T-62e66f7b
  './src/trading_platform/tickets/store.py'                     -> T-81475dff
  '/home/user/trading_platform/src/trading_platform/tickets/store.py' -> T-4af109ea
  'src/trading_platform/tickets/store.py:142'                   -> T-5c1573d9
  'tickets/store.py'                                            -> T-c37f2b90
Five tickets for one finding. Verified 2026-09-04.
title: Nothing validates a ticket's path: '', '/etc/passwd' and '../../' are accepted, and spelling variants of one file fork the id

detail:
IMPACT (P2): the log is the record and is append-only, so once such an event is written there is no sanctioned way to remove it - and sync_to_store TRUNCATEs then re-inserts everything, so ONE bad row means the projection can never be rebuilt again. `scripts/ticket.py sync` fails permanently and the operations view goes stale with no way back short of editing the append-only log, which the module docstring forbids.
Likelihood is low (it needs a pasted command or a mangled --path), but the recovery cost is the problem, not the frequency.
For contrast, a long ID is NOT reachable: _validate_filed forces ticket == ticket_id(...) which is always 10 chars, and a non-`filed` event with a long id is refused by fold as 'never filed' (verified 2026-09-04). It is `path` that is unbounded.
SUGGESTED FIX: bound path in _validate_filed (say 512 chars, with the same message style as the 160-char title rule), and/or index on left(path, 200) or use a hash index.
reproduction:
migrations/0005_tickets.sql creates `tickets_by_path` as a plain btree on tickets(path); btree version 4 caps an index row at 2704 bytes. Nothing bounds `path` on the Python side.
  p = 'src/' + secrets.token_hex(1500) + '.py'   # 3007 incompressible chars
  file_ticket(kind=FEATURE, severity=P3, title='long path', path=p, source='x', log=L)  # OK
  sync_to_store(conn, L)
Observed 2026-09-04 in throwaway schema ga_probe_2 (dropped):
  psycopg.errors.ProgramLimitExceeded: index row size 3024 exceeds btree version 4 maximum 2704 for index "tickets_by_path"
Same at 6007 chars. A compressible path of the same length succeeds, so the threshold depends on the content, not just the length.
title: A path over ~2700 bytes is accepted into the append-only log and then makes every sync fail forever

detail:
IMPACT (P2): test_an_event_round_trips_through_json's docstring claims 'Mutation: drop a field from to_json's loop - the round trip loses it'. It covers 7 of the 10 fields; 3 (resolution, commit, duplicate_of) are only reachable through other actions the test never builds, and duplicate_of is covered by nothing at all.
This matters because of what the missing coverage protects: if duplicate_of stopped being serialised, `scripts/ticket.py duplicate` would write a line that from_json reads back with duplicate_of='', which __post_init__ then refuses - so read_events raises and the ENTIRE LOG becomes unloadable for every command. A whole CLI subcommand (cmd_duplicate, ticket.py:129) and a whole fold branch (model.py:371) ship with zero tests; mutating that fold branch to leave the ticket OPEN also leaves the suite green (mutation S11, verified).
SUGGESTED FIX: one test that files two tickets, marks one a duplicate of the other through append(), reloads from disk, and asserts status is DUPLICATE, duplicate_of is the other id, and it is out of open_tickets(); plus a round-trip assertion over a `closed`, a `reopened` and a `duplicate` event, not only a `filed` one.
reproduction:
On a scratch copy of the tree (never the working tree), remove "duplicate_of" from the field loop in TicketEvent.to_json (src/trading_platform/tickets/model.py:213-224), then:
  PYTHONPATH=$MUT/src pytest tests/test_tickets.py tests/test_ticket_sync.py tests/test_store_guard.py -q
  -> 32 passed  (verified 2026-09-04)
The same mutation on "resolution" or "commit" IS caught, by test_ticket_sync.py::test_a_closed_ticket_leaves_the_open_list_and_keeps_its_history. Only duplicate_of survives. grep confirms no test anywhere constructs action='duplicate'.
title: The `duplicate` action is untested end to end: dropping duplicate_of from to_json leaves the whole ticket suite green

detail:
IMPACT (P3): the only call that passes a severity is test_the_repositorys_own_log_syncs' `assert len(open_from_store(conn, severity=['P0','P1'])) >= 1`, which is true whether or not the filter is applied - the log has 15 open tickets, so >= 1 holds unconditionally. The function's docstring says 'Open tickets from the projection, worst first' and nothing checks either half of that. open_from_store has no production consumer yet (it is 'for the operations page'), which is why this is P3 rather than P2 - the fake guard is on a function whose first user has not arrived.
SUGGESTED FIX: file a P0 and a P3 into a tmp log, sync, and assert [t['id'] for t in open_from_store(conn, severity=['P0'])] == [p0_id] and that an unfiltered call returns them P0-first.
reproduction:
On a scratch copy, in src/trading_platform/tickets/store.py:208-210 replace
    clauses.append("severity = ANY(%s)"); params.append(list(severity))
with `pass` (the severity argument is then ignored entirely), and separately replace
    " ORDER BY severity, opened_at" with "".
Then PYTHONPATH=$MUT/src pytest tests/test_tickets.py tests/test_ticket_sync.py tests/test_store_guard.py -q
  -> 32 passed for BOTH mutations (verified 2026-09-04, mutations S07b and S10).
title: open_from_store's severity filter and its worst-first ordering are unverified: deleting both leaves the ticket suite green

detail:
IMPACT (P3): the view is documented as 'by severity and kind', so the SQL is right and the test name is the thing that is wrong - but the test's shape means a caller who does `SELECT severity, tickets FROM open_debt ORDER BY severity` and reads rows[0][1] as 'how many P1s are open' gets a wrong number the moment two kinds share a severity, and no test would notice. This is a missing matrix cell (severity x kind), not a broken assertion.
SUGGESTED FIX: rename the test to say 'by severity and kind', and add the two-kinds-one-severity case asserting two rows summing to the total. If callers really want per-severity totals, add a second view or make them SUM().
reproduction:
migrations/0005_tickets.sql:89-99 has GROUP BY severity, kind. The test files three DEFECTs only, so every severity yields exactly one row and rows[0][1] happens to be the P1 count.
  file_ticket(kind=DEFECT,  severity=P1, title='a p1 defect',  path='a.py', ...)
  file_ticket(kind=FEATURE, severity=P1, title='a p1 feature', path='b.py', ...)
  sync_to_store(conn, log)
  SELECT severity, kind, tickets FROM open_debt ORDER BY severity, kind
Observed 2026-09-04 in throwaway schema ga_probe_3 (dropped):
  [('P1', 'defect', 1), ('P1', 'feature', 1)]
i.e. two rows for one severity, each counting 1, where the test's shape would read 1.
title: open_debt groups by (severity, kind), so the test named 'groups by severity' misses the cell where one severity has two kinds

detail:
IMPACT (P3): the file's own docstring says 'A new one added here and nowhere else is a suite that can go quiet unnoticed' - and the list itself is the thing nothing guards. This is corpus entry G02 one level up: the guard is real, but the enumeration it guards is hand-copied, which is the same defect class as the hand-maintained TECHNICAL_DEBT.md that the ticket mechanism just replaced.
SUGGESTED FIX: derive the list instead of writing it - glob tests/test_*.py, import each, and treat any module whose pytestmark mentions TRADING_PLATFORM_TEST_DSN as store-backed; assert that set equals STORE_BACKED_MODULES so adding a module fails loudly until it is listed. This needs confirming for cost (importing every test module) before it is done.
reproduction:
On a scratch copy, delete the line '    "tests.test_ticket_sync",' from STORE_BACKED_MODULES (tests/test_store_guard.py:43), then PYTHONPATH=$MUT/src pytest tests/ -q.
Nothing goes red: the guard simply stops policing that module, after which tests/test_ticket_sync.py could be set to skip unconditionally against a live database and the suite would still report green. (Setting that module's pytestmark to skipif(True) WITH the entry present is correctly caught - mutation G01, verified 2026-09-04.)
title: STORE_BACKED_MODULES is a hand-maintained list with no guard, so a store-backed suite can be dropped from the guard silently

detail:
IMPACT (P3): low today because the CLI always stamps datetime.now(UTC) and the only other writer is a backfill. It matters when two agents' clocks disagree, when a backfill is replayed, or when someone reconstructs history - the debt table then shows a 'since' date later than the closure, and 'how long was this P1 open' becomes negative with nothing raising. sync_to_store orders ticket_events by BIGSERIAL (file order), so the projection inherits the same disagreement between row order and `at`.
It also interacts with the re-file-does-not-reopen defect: an out-of-order re-file already reads as corroboration on a closed ticket regardless of when it happened.
SUGGESTED FIX: refuse, in fold(), an event whose `at` precedes the ticket's last recorded event - consistent with this repository's 'refuse rather than assume' rule - or at minimum record it as a note so the disorder is visible rather than silently averaged into the dates.
reproduction:
fold() replays in file order and never compares `at` between events; file_ticket accepts an arbitrary `at`.
  i,_ = file_ticket(kind=FEATURE, severity=P2, title='f', path='a.py', source='a', at=T0, log=L)
  append([TicketEvent(ticket=i, action='closed', at=T0 - timedelta(days=30), source='b',
                      resolution='closed before it was opened')], L)
  t = load(L)[i]
Observed 2026-09-04: opened_at=2026-09-01T12:00Z, closed_at=2026-08-02T12:00Z, closed_at < opened_at is True, no error, no note.
title: fold() accepts events out of chronological order and produces a ticket closed before it was opened, with no complaint

resolution: fold() now reopens a ticket re-filed while closed, bumps reopens and notes it; the CLI says REOPENED. Tests: test_re_filing_a_closed_finding_reopens_it, test_re_filing_an_already_open_finding_does_not_count_as_a_reopen

file_ticket reads and appends under one exclusive flock and records a read failure instead of raising, so a torn read can never cost the finding; each record is written in one os.write to an O_APPEND fd. Tests: test_a_read_failure_never_costs_the_finding, test_concurrent_filers_all_land_and_the_log_stays_parseable

detail: Only to compute is_new and previous_status. Harmless at hundreds of tickets, quadratic beyond. Fix: index the last status per ticket id, or read only the tail.
reproduction: 6 processes x 4 file_ticket calls with 60KB details took over 120s before the log was trimmed; each call folds every prior event to compute one boolean
title: file_ticket re-parses the whole log on every call, so filing is quadratic in log size

detail: The mechanisms exist and are tested; the production entrypoint does not use them. Needs a --dsn/--stage wiring and the account's gate built from store.accounts.leverage_gate. Found by adversarial-reviewer 2026-09-04 (F4).
reproduction: grep -n 'tracker\|leverage_gate' scripts/run_paper.py returns nothing; a real paper run therefore writes no account_marks and gates no leverage, while the tests wire both by hand
title: scripts/run_paper.py passes neither a tracker nor a leverage gate

resolution: run_paper.py now builds the tracker and the account's leverage gate from the store and passes both, records the stage, and REFUSES a leveraged account with no store rather than warning. Tests: tests/test_run_paper_wiring.py (4), both mutations verified red.

normalise_path canonicalises at construction (leading ./, doubled slashes, a :LINE suffix, surrounding space); _validate_path refuses empty, absolute and ..-escaping paths. Five spellings are one ticket again; the 21 paths already in the log were canonical, so no existing id moved.

PATH_MAX = 512 bytes, enforced in _validate_path, well under the 2704-byte btree index row limit. Counted in bytes, not characters: a 400-character non-ASCII path exceeds the index limit while passing a character count.

Every rendered cell now goes through _cell(), which escapes | and collapses whitespace; a line break in a title or a path is refused at the source by _validate_single_line. Tested with a pipe in the title, the path and the resolution, and with a resolution that wraps.

duplicate is covered end to end (file two, mark one a duplicate, reload from disk, assert status, duplicate_of and absence from open_tickets), plus a round trip over closed, wontfix, reopened, duplicate and note. cmd_duplicate now refuses an unknown --of and a self-reference.

detail: The one code path whose entire job is 'the database is down, say so rather than rendering zeros' fails with a second, unrelated exception. The operations page 500s and check_health.py exits 1 with a traceback rather than the reason. Found by running the new health check against a database one migration behind.
reproduction: TRADING_PLATFORM_DSN pointed at a database missing a migration, then scripts/check_health.py: 'AttributeError: OpsSnapshot object has no attribute __dict__'. OpsSnapshot is slots=True, so `empty.__dict__` in the except branch cannot work. Every test of this branch constructs OpsSnapshot(error=...) by hand, so the branch itself has never run.
title: read_snapshot's store-unreachable path raises AttributeError instead of reporting

resolution: read_snapshot's except branch now uses dataclasses.replace instead of **empty.__dict__, and a test drives the real path with a connection whose cursor() raises — the branch had never once run, because every test of it built OpsSnapshot(error=...) by hand. Corpus entry W01.

A capture heartbeats its live counters onto its own open ingest_runs row every poll (migration 0007, heartbeat_at + stats, view collector_health), swallowed so an observer cannot kill what it observes. web/ops.assess() turns a snapshot into ALARM/WARN alerts; the page's headline is derived from it and scripts/check_health.py exits non-zero on it, so one definition of healthy serves both. deploy/trading-health.{service,timer} run it every five minutes. Corpus entry W02.

Answered by refusing the mislabelling rather than by paying for SIP: run_collector.validate now rejects a config whose venue contradicts its feed tier (TAPE_BY_FEED), so Alpaca's free IEX feed cannot be stamped 'sip'. Labelled honestly it lands in the cross-venue bucket, where the reconciler already reports it as basis rather than as an error rate. The IEX-to-consolidated spread is then measured under its own name, which is worth having and is not data validation. Vendors whose tiers nobody has checked are left alone rather than guessed at.

detail: The merged worst-subset model measures the entry as though the flatten might not fill, which is true of a limit order and false of a market one; the risk layer cannot tell them apart. This is a false REJECTION, not a hole, and it was chosen deliberately at the merge: committing pending orders instead was measured and took the working-order breach from none back to 2x the position cap. target_notional (ADR 0008) emits exactly this flatten+entry pair, so a flip now takes two instants instead of one. Fixing it needs a way to distinguish a marketable order from a resting one at check time — a real design question, not a constant to loosen.
reproduction: RiskLimits(max_order_notional=5000, max_position_notional=1500); long 100 at 100. submit sell 100 (flatten) -> True. submit sell 12 (1,200 of notional, cap 1,500) -> False, reason position_notional. See tests/test_risk_composition.py::test_a_flip_to_a_smaller_opposite_side_is_measured_by_every_size_cap.
title: A flatten and the entry behind it cannot pass in one batch

detail: R04's original consequence (a halted account re-entering against a phantom short) is now prevented by construction and R04 is declared a survivor on that evidence. What release_filled still prevents is a false REJECTION from double-counted gross exposure, and nothing covers it. A test was attempted and withdrawn rather than shipped green: pending deltas clear at every instant, so the double count is only reachable within one instant, and the engine paths that fill inside an instant (on_cross_section) could not be made to express it in the time available. Either find that path and guard it, or establish that it is unreachable through the engine and narrow release_filled's contract to say so.
reproduction: Replace 'risk.release_filled(fill)' in engine/backtester.py with 'pass' and run the full suite: 1307 passed. detail: The test asserts the plan's central claim -- that the train/test split is enforced by the type system rather than a comment -- by type-checking a snippet that swaps TrainWindow and TestWindow, and requiring exactly two mypy errors. Off that one machine subprocess.run raises before mypy starts, so the guard has never executed here. Note the failure mode is an error rather than a skip, so it is loud -- but it means CI on origin has been unable to pass this test since 885ab30. detail: The claim the test makes -- 'float does not accumulate cleanly across many fills, which is the failure mode that makes a run impossible to reconcile' -- is still TRUE; it is the demonstration that broke. A ledger accumulates with a running +=, not with builtin sum(), and 0.1 added ten times is still 0.9999999999999999 on 3.12. The test should demonstrate the accumulation a ledger actually performs. Left as sum() it is worse than wrong: on 3.12 it asserts that float accumulates cleanly, which is the opposite of the invariant the repository is built on. Surfaced by the 3.11/3.12 split between CI and the development venv.
reproduction: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_cache.py::test_float_would_have_lost_this -q  ->  'assert 1.0 != 1.0' on Python 3.12.13. Python 3.12 gave builtin sum() Neumaier compensated summation, so sum([0.1] * 10) == 1.0 exactly. Passes on 3.11 (what CI installs), fails on 3.12 (what .venv and .python-version carried), so the outcome depends on the interpreter.

The fixture builds a throwaway repo and commits into it with -c user.email and -c user.name overridden, but not commit.gpgsign. git therefore reads the developer's GLOBAL signing config and tries to sign a scratch commit with their real key. Three consequences: the suite depends on an unlocked credential agent, which makes it non-deterministic in a way nothing in the output explains; it invokes the user's signing key for a test that has nothing to do with signing; and it fails on any machine where signing is configured but the key is unavailable. The test is about check-defaults.sh, so the fix is to pass -c commit.gpgsign=false alongside the identity overrides already there. Same class as T-23095c48 and T-0fb1e86b: the authoring environment's properties leaking into the test.
reproduction: With commit.gpgsign=true and gpg.format=ssh in the user's global git config (gpg.ssh.program=/opt/1Password/op-ssh-sign), lock 1Password and run: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_check_defaults_hook.py -q  ->  ERROR ... 'error: 1Password: failed to fill whole buffer / fatal: failed to write commit object' from the repo fixture's 'git commit -qm base'. Observed live: the whole suite went from green to one ERROR when the agent locked partway through a session, with no code change.
title: The defaults-hook test signs its scratch commit with the developer's real signing key, so a locked agent turns the suite red

resolution: Both scratch-repo fixtures now set commit.gpgsign=false (and tag.gpgsign=false in the hook test) alongside the identity they were already overriding. test_experiment_records.py had the same latent coupling in two fixtures and was fixed with it. Found live when the developer's 1Password agent locked mid-session and the suite went red with an error naming 1Password rather than the test.

detail: The eval copies the tree to a scratch directory and does NOT copy .venv. The new test invoked deploy/install.sh with --prefix pointing at the copy, and install.sh hardcoded PYTHON=$PREFIX/.venv/bin/python, so preflight found no interpreter and exited 2. Consequence is out of proportion to the cause: the eval aborts entirely when its control fails, by design, so between 4854f5f and the fix the repository's level-1 defence measured nothing at all. A guard that disables the harness measuring every other guard is the same shape as the guards this project keeps finding -- green by absence. Fixed on both sides: install.sh gained --python (the venv is not always inside the prefix, which is a real deployment case and not just a test artefact), and the test passes sys.executable. Verified against a deliberately venv-less copy of the tree.
reproduction: At 4854f5f: .venv/bin/python scripts/run_mutation_eval.py --jobs 2  ->  'ABORTING: the suite does not pass on an unmutated tree' after 14s, with test_deploy_units.py failing on 'MISSING interpreter /tmp/mutation-eval-*/CONTROL/.venv/bin/python'. Reproduce without the eval by copying the tree WITHOUT .venv and running the file against it.
title: A new guard aborted the mutation eval's control run, switching off the harness that measures every other guard

resolution: install.sh gained --python (default $PREFIX/.venv/bin/python), because an interpreter outside the prefix is a real deployment case rather than only a test artefact; tests/test_deploy_units.py passes sys.executable. Verified by copying the tree without .venv, as the eval does, and running the file against it: 15 passed. The eval's control now passes and the full run proceeds.

detail: Alpaca is now HALF verified, and the half matters. Alpaca's crypto bars endpoint (/v1beta3/crypto/us/bars) requires no credentials -- confirmed 200 with real BTC/USD data -- so data/alpaca.py was checked against a real response without waiting for a key. Wire shape is exactly what the module's docstring assumes: t/o/h/l/c/v plus n and vw, prices as JSON floats. Decimal(str(x)) exact for every field. OHLC internally consistent. Critically, every bar is stamped at wire-t PLUS the timeframe -- wire t=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z renders as 2026-09-02T00:00:00+00:00 -- so the open-stamped/close-stamped confusion that is corpus defect D01 does not occur against real data. Both AlpacaParseError guards fire (a symbol present but not requested, and a payload with no 'bars'). STILL UNVERIFIED and still needing a key: live/alpaca.py in its entirety -- the auth headers, the pagination loop (note a 5-row page already returns a non-null next_page_token, so paging is not hypothetical), and the poller that withholds the bar in progress -- plus the stocks endpoint, whose feed and adjustment parameters have no crypto equivalent and are therefore untested. Note live/alpaca.py:172 calls require_all() unconditionally, so the client demands both keys even for the public crypto path; that is defensible (keys buy rate limit) but it is why the transport could not be tested here.

Consequence, and the failure mode is well-behaved but total: poll_once catches the fetch exception, counts it, increments consecutive_errors and returns 0. The capture therefore stays alive, records nothing forever, and check_health.py correctly ALARMs. Nothing is silent -- but the collector cannot capture from a delayed feed at all, and Polygon's free tier is delayed by ~15 minutes. Delayed data is a normal vendor tier, not an exotic case. Proposed fix: a 'delay: timedelta = timedelta(0)' on CaptureConfig, with the window end computed as now - delay and the value recorded on the source, so a reader can see that a feed is deliberately behind rather than broken. Note this is a REQUEST-WINDOW change, not a change to bar ordering or to due_bars, and it must not become a way to backdate a bar: the bars themselves keep their own timestamps. It also interacts with feed_health's silent_for, which would otherwise read a deliberate 15-minute lag as a fault. Not implemented here: whether a delayed source should participate in same-venue reconciliation at all is a design question, since it changes what 'the sources disagree' means.
reproduction: With a valid Polygon FREE-tier key: PolygonMarketData(...).fetch_symbol('AAPL','1m', now-2h, now-5min) -> TransportError HTTP 403. The same call with end=2026-09-05 (historical) returns 573 bars, so the key and the path are fine; it is the recency of the window END that is refused. CaptureConfig.poll_once builds 'bars = self.fetcher.fetch_bars(self.symbols, self.interval, since, now)' with now = self.clock(), and there is no field that offsets the end, so every poll asks for data the tier will not serve.

title: A capture always requests a window ending at now, so a delayed vendor 403s on every poll and can never record a bar

detail: The file is the one docs/SETUP.md and docs/RUNBOOK.md both tell you to copy as your starting point, so the documented first run rate-limits itself on the documented free tier. It fails visibly -- 429 is counted as a fetch error and consecutive_errors climbs -- so this is a bad first experience rather than a silent wrong number, which is why it is P3 and not higher. Worth noting alongside T-73a2d1bc, which is the harder half: even at an acceptable poll rate, a free-tier Polygon capture 403s on every poll because the window ends at now. Fix is a comment in the example naming the free-tier limits per vendor, and a poll_every_s that does not exceed them by default; a config that works on the free tier is the right default when the free tier is what SETUP.md tells you to sign up for.

detail: Crypto has a complete ingestion path: scripts/fetch_binance.py writes klines and funding into the Parquet cache, store_load_cache.py loads the cache into Postgres and proves the round trip. Equities have neither half. The only Polygon entry point in scripts/ is run_collector.py, which is LIVE capture -- and T-73a2d1bc establishes that a free-tier Polygon key 403s on every live poll because poll_once always requests a window ending at now. So the net position is that data/polygon.py and live/polygon.py are both VERIFIED on the wire (2026-09-08, 9 daily and 31 1m AAPL bars, close-stamping and Decimal conversion exact) and there is still no way to get a single equity bar into the store or the cache. Proposed: scripts/fetch_polygon.py following the shape of fetch_binance.py -- symbol, interval, start, end, writing to the Parquet cache via data/cache.write_bars, reusing PolygonMarketData.fetch_symbol which already pages and refuses cross-origin redirects. Two things it must get right that fetch_binance did not have to: the market key is equity or etf and the two are separate in cache.MARKETS (SPY is an ETF, AAPL is not), and the free tier's ~5 requests/minute needs deliberate pacing rather than a retry storm. It must also stay well clear of the recency window that returns 403.
title: There is no path to get equity data into the platform: Polygon has no historical fetch script and its free tier cannot feed the collector

resolution: scripts/fetch_polygon.py added, mirroring fetch_binance.py. Verified end to end on real data: 67 AAPL daily bars into data/cache/equity/AAPL/1d.parquet and 67 SPY bars into data/cache/etf/SPY/1d.parquet, then store_load_cache.py --market equity reported IDENTICAL on the bar-for-bar round trip through Postgres. Data-quality checks pass: no duplicates, strictly increasing, tz-aware, no future stamps, OHLC consistent, no zero-volume bars, and the only gaps longer than a weekend are 2026-06-19 (Juneteenth) and 2026-07-03 (Independence Day observed) -- which independently confirms both the data and the close-stamping convention, since a bar stamped D covers session D-1. The script is shaped by the three free-tier facts measured on 2026-09-08: --end defaults to 20 minutes ago because the tier 403s on newer data, requests are paced 13s apart rather than retried because the tier allows ~5/minute, and --market is required with no default because equity and etf are separate cache keys. 12 tests, network-free. T-73a2d1bc (live capture against a delayed vendor) is NOT closed by this -- backfill and live capture are different problems.

detail: This is the silent-wrong-number class, and it is worse than a 403 because it succeeds. A researcher asks for five years, is told '499 bars', and runs a walk-forward over what they believe is five years of data. Every window count, every fold boundary and every out-of-sample claim downstream is then computed over a different dataset than the one named in the experiment record -- and charter 85 dataset ids would record the REQUESTED range unless something compares it to what arrived. Note it also interacts badly with merge_bars: repeated runs with different --start values would leave a cache whose coverage nobody can state from the file alone. The fix belongs in fetch_polygon.py rather than in the adapter, because it is a property of the ACCOUNT and not of the wire format: compare the first bar returned against the requested start and refuse, or at minimum warn loudly with both dates and the shortfall in days. 'A gap is a gap' and 'refuse rather than assume' both point the same way here. Related: T-73a2d1bc (same tier refuses recent data) and T-d2d4e55a (same tier's rate limit) -- three separate ways one free plan differs from its own API reference.
reproduction: scripts/fetch_polygon.py AAPL --market equity --interval 1d --start 2021-01-01 --end 2026-09-04  ->  '499 bars', first bar 2024-09-10. Requested span 5.7 years, delivered span 1.98 years, 1348 days of requested history dropped. Identical truncation on all five symbols tried (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, SPY, QQQ), all landing on the same first date, which is what identifies it as a plan limit rather than a listing date. HTTP 200 throughout: no error, no warning, no next_url, nothing in the payload saying the window was cut.
title: Polygon's free tier silently truncates the requested window to ~2 years, and nothing notices

resolution: fetch_polygon.py now compares the first bar returned against the requested start and REFUSES (exit 2, nothing written) when the gap exceeds TRUNCATION_GRACE_DAYS = 10. The grace is set against calendar reasons rather than against a documented plan limit, because the limit is a property of the account and moves when the plan does: a long weekend is 4 days and the longest US market closure in living memory was 6 (September 2001), while a plan limit costs years. --allow-short keeps the shorter window deliberately. Verified against the real key: the request that silently returned 2 years now prints 'REFUSED: asked for 2021-01-01, earliest bar is 2024-09-10 - 1348 days short' and writes nothing, while a request inside the plan's reach still succeeds. Four tests, both mutations killed (guard removed -> 2 dead; grace widened to 10 years -> 3 dead).

detail: CORRECTION to an earlier note in this ticket. Coinbase was recorded as 403/geoblocked; that was wrong. api.exchange.coinbase.com returns 200 for public candles once a User-Agent header is set -- urllib's default UA is what was refused. Kraken also answers 200 keyless. Polygon serves crypto aggregates (X:BTCUSD) on the same stocks key already verified. So the keyless/available crypto sources are now: Binance (VERIFIED, klines and funding), Alpaca crypto (parser verified via the public endpoint), Coinbase (reachable, no adapter), Kraken (reachable, no adapter), Polygon (reachable on an existing verified adapter). _as_source(series) converts a MacroSeries into a Source and keeps its id, on the stated assumption that 'a macro series carries the same identity'. It does not: macro_series and sources are different tables with independent id sequences, and ingest_runs.source_id is a foreign key into sources. So the id is not a shared identity, it is a coincidence, and the failure mode depends entirely on how many bar sources happen to exist. With FEWER bar sources than macro series it raises, which is what happened here on the third series and is the loud, harmless case. With AS MANY OR MORE it silently attributes macro ingest runs to market-data sources and writes. That is the case that matters: charter 10 and store/__init__.py both state that a fact in this database is always attributable -- which source said it, which run fetched it, when it landed -- and this makes that false without any error. Note scripts/run_collector.py does it correctly, calling ensure_source() to register its source before opening a run; fetch_macro.py never calls ensure_source at all. Fix: ensure_source(conn, name='fred', kind='vendor') once, and use that Source for ingest_run, keeping MacroSeries for what it is. Separately, the two already-written runs need deciding about: the observations themselves are correct and correctly linked to macro_series, so this is repairable by repointing source_id rather than by deleting data.
reproduction: With a valid FRED_API_KEY and two bar sources already in the store (ids 1 and 2): .venv/bin/python scripts/fetch_macro.py --series GDP UNRATE CPIAUCSL  ->  GDP is written under ingest_run 4 with source_id=1, which is 'binance-equity'; UNRATE under run 5 with source_id=2, 'binance-etf'; CPIAUCSL then crashes with psycopg.errors.ForeignKeyViolation because no sources row has id 3. Verified in the database afterwards: 3,241 GDP and 2,198 UNRATE observations landed under runs attributed to market-data sources they have nothing to do with.
title: fetch_macro.py attributes every macro ingest run to an unrelated market-data source, because it reuses a macro_series id as a sources id

detail: Two separate hardcodings on adjacent lines. Line 68: name = args.source or f'binance-{args.market}', so the DEFAULT source name asserts a vendor. Line 93: venue='binance' is not a parameter at all, so it cannot be overridden even deliberately. The --source help text says 'default <market>-cache', which is a third disagreement -- the help describes behaviour the code does not have. Severity is P1 because venue is the field the entire reconciliation model rests on. docs/RUNBOOK.md: 'venue is a thing you declare, and getting it wrong is the easiest way to make this useless... stamping it with the vendor made every Alpaca-versus-Polygon gap read as basis, so every genuine error became a shrug.' The collector was fixed to refuse a source that declares no venue (run_collector.py:134); this loader was not, and it declares a wrong one instead, which is worse than declaring none because nothing can detect it. A same_venue comparison between these rows and a real Binance source would treat US equity prices and crypto prices as the same tape. Fix: --venue required with no default when --source is not given, or derived from the market, and the help text corrected. The 2,495 already-loaded bars carry the wrong venue and need a decision -- the prices are correct, only the attribution is wrong, so this is repairable rather than requiring deletion. Sibling of T-c5a8f437, found in the same hour: both are provenance defects in scripts that write to the store, and both went unnoticed because nothing had run them against data from a second vendor.
reproduction: scripts/fetch_polygon.py AAPL --market equity ... then scripts/store_load_cache.py --market equity --interval 1d. Query afterwards: select s.name, s.venue, b.market, count(*) from bars b join sources s on s.id=b.source_id group by 1,2,3  ->  'binance-equity | binance | equity | 1497' for AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, and 'binance-etf | binance | etf | 998' for SPY, QQQ. Every one of those bars is Polygon's, from US exchanges, and none of them has anything to do with Binance.
title: store_load_cache.py hardcodes venue='binance' and names every source 'binance-<market>', so Polygon equity bars claim to have traded on Binance

resolution: fetch_macro.py now calls ensure_source(conn, 'fred', kind='vendor') once and uses that Source for every ingest run; _as_source() is deleted rather than left to be reused. Verified: runs 7, 8 and 9 are attributed to 'fred', and CPIAUCSL -- which previously crashed with a ForeignKeyViolation -- fetched 3,361 observations over 955 periods and 668 vintages. The two already-written runs (4 GDP under binance-equity, 5 UNRATE under binance-etf) are NOT touched by this fix and are left for a human decision, since an ingest run is a provenance record and charter 69 requires an explicit decision before one is changed or deleted.

--vendor and --venue are now both required on store_load_cache.py, with no default and nothing inferred; the source name is built from --vendor, and the --source help text no longer describes behaviour the code does not have. DATA DECISION, taken explicitly by the repository's owner on 2026-09-08 under charter 69 and recorded here because it was a deletion: the 2,495 bars stamped venue='binance' that were Polygon's, their three import runs, and the two sources binance-equity and binance-etf were DELETED, after the identical prices had been reloaded as polygon-equity and polygon-etf with venue='sip' and verified IDENTICAL on the bar-for-bar round trip. Nothing correct was destroyed: the 3,241 GDP and 2,198 UNRATE macro observations that hung off the mis-attributed fetch-fred runs were REPOINTED onto the fred runs for the same series rather than deleted, because the observations were right and only their attribution was wrong. Store after: polygon-equity venue=sip 2,495 bars, polygon-etf venue=sip 1,996 bars, three macro series all under fred. The full account of what went wrong stays in this ticket and in KNOWN_FAILURES.md -- what was removed is the false rows, not the record of them.

detail: Coinbase returns the in-progress bucket like any other candle, with no flag marking it unclosed. data/binance.py already solves this exactly right -- klines_to_bars takes drop_forming and an INJECTED now_ms, and its docstring says why the injection matters: the engine never reads wall time, and an injected value is what makes forming-bar rejection testable at all. data/coinbase.py has neither, so the partial bar is written to the Parquet cache as final. A backtest reading that cache uses a fraction of a day's range and volume as a complete day, at the most recent bar -- the one most likely to matter to whatever prompted the fetch. It also poisons merge_bars: incoming wins on conflict, so re-running later correctly replaces it, but any result computed in between is wrong and nothing records that it was. Same class as the Alpaca poller's withheld-bar handling, which live/alpaca.py already does. Fix: bars_from_payload takes now and drop_forming, dropping any bar whose close timestamp exceeds now; CoinbaseMarketData takes a clock like CaptureConfig does.
reproduction: scripts/fetch_coinbase.py BTC-USD --interval 1d --start 2026-08-01 --end 2026-09-08 writes 39 bars, the newest stamped 2026-09-09T00:00Z -- a close time in the FUTURE, because it covers the session that began today and has not ended. Comparing the stored bars against an independent raw request minutes later: 38/39 identical, and the newest disagrees on close (78445.91 vs 78452.80) and volume (3060.55 vs 3303.44), because the candle is still moving.
title: The Coinbase adapter stores the still-forming candle as though it were closed

resolution: bars_from_payload now takes an injected 'now' and 'drop_forming=True', dropping any candle whose close timestamp is in the future; CoinbaseMarketData takes a 'clock' like CaptureConfig does, so nothing here reads wall time directly and the rejection is testable. Follows data/binance.py's klines_to_bars exactly, including why the clock is injected. Three tests added; the mutation that removes the guard kills two of them. Verified against the live API: a fetch into a clean cache now returns 38 bars ending on the last CLOSED day, against 39 ending on a bar stamped in the future before the fix. SECOND-ORDER PROPERTY WORTH KNOWING, found while verifying this: a forming bar that is ALREADY cached survives the fix, because merge_bars keeps an existing entry that is absent from 'incoming' -- and a withheld bar is absent by construction. The cache self-heals only once that candle closes and a later fetch returns it as final. Any cache written before this fix therefore holds one partial bar until then; the one written in this session was deleted and refetched rather than left to heal.
